recognize_zh: 骨髓抹片中一顆大型巨核細胞旁邊，有胞質充滿大小不等透明空泡的泡沫狀組織球（foamy histiocytes），吞入細胞看不出來，屬非特異性的反應性變化，需配合臨床考慮儲積症等原因。
features: Large histiocytes with abundant cytoplasm filled with numerous clear vacuoles of varying size (foamy/soap-bubble appearance)
Small nuclei partly obscured by vacuoles
Adjacent large megakaryocyte with lobulated nucleus and granular cytoplasm for size comparison
No engulfed hematopoietic cells or organisms evident within the histiocytes
Background of red cells and a few maturing myeloid cells
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows histiocytes with abundant cytoplasm distended by numerous clear vacuoles of variable size, lying beside a normal-appearing megakaryocyte. No hemophagocytosis, microorganisms or crystalline inclusions are identified. Foamy histiocytes are a nonspecific finding and may be seen after chemotherapy, in marrow injury, hyperlipidemia or lipid storage disorders. In a child with suspected lysosomal storage disease, correlation with enzyme assays (e.g., acid sphingomyelinase) and genetic testing is recommended.

ddx.vs: Niemann-Pick cells show uniform fine foamy vacuolation across many histiocytes; morphology alone cannot distinguish them from reactive foamy macrophages without enzyme assay.
Gaucher cells have fibrillary crumpled-paper cytoplasm rather than discrete clear vacuoles.
Hemophagocytosis shows engulfed red cells, platelets or nucleated cells within the macrophage cytoplasm, which are not seen here.
